claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first assessment question for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first question about your child:

**How old is the child you're asking about?**

To help me assess your eligibility, I need to know:

- Is the child **under 16 years old**?
- Is the child **between 16-19 years old**?
- Or is the child **20 years old or over**?

This will determine which eligibility path we need to follow.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and want to check if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 8 years old, so he falls into the **under 16** category. Let me proceed with the next step of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news so far! Since Alex is under 16, we need to check one important criterion:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

This is relevant because children who work 24 or more hours per week may have different eligibility rules. Since Alex is only 8 years old, I expect the answer is yes, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh no, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8! He's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected. Since Alex is 8 years old and not working, he definitely meets this requirement. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask about benefits:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

For an 8-year-old in primary school, this is unlikely, but I need to confirm that Alex is not receiving any of these benefits on their own.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I'd expect for an 8-year-old. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to ask about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Given that Alex is only 8 years old and in primary school, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm. If he is in an apprenticeship, there are specific regional rules that would apply (different rules for England, Scotland, and Wales).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8 years old and in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense. Since Alex is not in any apprenticeship, let me continue to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency status, which is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you meet any of the following UK residency requirements?**

1. **Normally live in the UK** - You reside in the UK as your normal home
2. **Settled status under EU Settlement Scheme** - You have settled status under the EUSS
3. **Pre-settled status and working** - You have pre-settled status and are working, earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months
4. **Pre-settled status and actively seeking work** - You have pre-settled status and are looking for work (up to 91 days as jobseeker)
5. **Pre-settled status with sufficient resources** - You have pre-settled status, sufficient resources to support yourself and family, and are NOT claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit
6. **Pre-settled status as a student** - You have pre-settled status, are studying, and have sufficient resources
7. **Pre-settled status as family member of EEA/Swiss national** - You have pre-settled status and are a family member (spouse, dependent child/grandchild, or dependent parent/grandparent) of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside
8. **Crown servant living abroad** - You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to you, or do you normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I live in Manchester. That's my normal home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward. You meet the residency requirement by normally living in the UK. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to confirm that you are responsible for Alex. "Responsibility" can be established in several ways:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **Living with the child** - You live with Alex
2. **Contributing to their upkeep** - You pay at least the equivalent of Child Benefit (or provide equivalent support in kind) towards Alex's care, including things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents
3. **Paying maintenance** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement that covers Alex's upkeep and equals or exceeds the Child Benefit payment

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards his upkeep - things like clothes and helping with other expenses.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So you're contributing financially to Alex's upkeep through things like clothes and other expenses, even though Alex doesn't live with you.

To proceed, I need to understand a bit more about the level of your contribution:

**Are you paying at least the equivalent amount of Child Benefit towards Alex's upkeep?**

For context, Child Benefit is currently £25.60 per week for the first child (though this can vary). Your contributions—whether weekly, monthly, or as lump sums—should equal or exceed this amount to establish responsibility through the contribution route.

Are your contributions to Alex's clothes and other expenses at this level or higher?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's needs, so that covers things like his clothes and other expenses.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear then. You're contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which exceeds the Child Benefit threshold. This means you meet the responsibility requirement through financial contribution. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Important question now:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone applied to claim Child Benefit for him?**

This could be:
- Alex's other parent
- Another relative or carer who also lives with or contributes to Alex's upkeep
- Anyone else

Please let me know if there are other potential claimants involved.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Since there's no other claimant for Alex, let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check on Alex's living situation:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

1. **In hospital** - Is Alex in hospital care?
2. **In care** - Is Alex in local authority care (e.g., children's home)?
3. **Fostered** - Is Alex being fostered?
4. **Normal living** - Is Alex living in a normal home (with family, relatives, or other normal living arrangement)?

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living in a normal home situation - he lives with his other parent.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good! So Alex is living in a normal home situation with his other parent. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council providing any financial support towards where Alex lives or his upkeep? Or is his accommodation and maintenance being paid for privately by you and/or his other parent?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - Alex lives with his other parent and we handle everything privately between us.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final check completed. You've met all the eligibility requirements. Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Congratulations! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit** ✓

---

### Summary for Alex:

**Result:** ✅ **ELIGIBLE**

**Why you qualify:**
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16 - a qualifying age)
- Alex is not working full-time
- Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right
- You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- **You are responsible for Alex** through regular financial contributions of £30 per week towards his upkeep (clothes, expenses, etc.)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is living in a normal home situation with his other parent
- The local council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

---

### What You Should Do Next:

1. **Apply for Child Benefit** if you haven't already done so:
   - Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
   - You can apply online, by phone, or by post

2. **You'll need to provide:**
   - Your National Insurance number
   - Details about Alex (name, date of birth, National Insurance number if he has one)
   - Evidence of your responsibility for Alex (such as bank statements showing your £30 weekly contributions)

3. **Payment:** If approved, Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks directly into your bank account.

If you have any questions about the application process or need further support, you can contact HMRC's Child Benefit helpline on **0300 200 3100**.

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding Child Benefit?
